Hi Lee —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discussion and proposed next steps so we have alignment for the evaluation. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- Intermittent p95 latency spikes on batch inference during peak traffic (~300–600ms today, target <200ms).
- High variable token cost across pipelines; team is trying to bring per-1M-token spend down without sacrificing latency.
- Cold start and KV-cache warmup hurting short-session UX in your contextual search product.
- Need for deterministic-ish outputs for A/B experiments and fair comparison across providers.

Current stack you described:
- Models served via a vLLM + TGI stack on GCP (k8s, auto-scaling).
- Mix of quantized Llama 2 70B and an internal tuned 13B variant for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Prefix caching in-app; limited model-side KV sharing today.

Success criteria for the bake-off (as we captured) — please confirm:
- Performance: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for 1–2k token contexts for the 13B baseline; throughput >= 100 req/s on peak benchmark.
- Cost: total inference cost <= current baseline (you quoted ~$1200 per 1M effective tokens) — target relative reduction 20%+.
- Quality/regression: similarity on your eval set (we’ll use your JSONL) with no >5% drop in top-1 accuracy for the classification prompts; low regression on hallucination tests.
- Reliability/SLO: 99.9% availability during the trial window and graceful fallback to smaller variants under load.

Benchmarks we propose to run (please confirm/adjust):
1) Latency sweep: 1–5 concurrent clients, contexts of 512/1K/2K tokens, record p50/p95/p99 and tail token latencies.
2) Throughput plateau: increase QPS to find stable throughput on a dedicated Redwood pool equivalent.
3) Cost simulation: run identical prompts across environments to compute cost per effective token and normalized cost per 1M tokens.
4) Quality checks: run your acme_js_eval_set.jsonl (attached) for top-1 accuracy, BLEU/ROUGE samples (as applicable), and hallucination detection.
5) Cold-start/kv warmup: measure first-request latency distribution vs warmed KV cache.

Comparators you asked for: we will provide runs vs vLLM (your current baseline), TGI endpoints, and a cloud-hosted endpoint (we'll use a configured managed endpoint representative of "cloud" — see matrix in attachment). We will include notes about quantization/precision variants we test.

What we need from you to kick this off:
- Confirm acceptance numbers above or send your constraints (latency/cost/quality) by EOD Friday.
- Agree on the eval shard from acme_js_eval_set.jsonl to use as the canonical test set (attached).
- Provide a small sample of production traffic patterns (RPS profile) or a synthetic generator so we match real-world bursts.
- Approve a 2-hour kick-off slot next week for test orchestration and infra access.

Proposed timeline:
- Day 0: Exchange eval dataset & test account credentials.
- Days 1–2: Redwood runs initial baseline & latency sweep.
- Days 3–5: Throughput runs + cost simulations + quality checks.
- Day 7: Readout + decision/next steps.

Attachments: acme_js_eval_set.jsonl (sample eval set) — please confirm this is the canonical set.

Next steps (asks): please reply to confirm the acceptance criteria and availability for the kick-off (I’ve suggested 90–120 minute window). Once confirmed we’ll push the trial run instructions and pre-built scripts (redwood_trial_run_instructions.pdf) to the Drive link.

Thanks — looking forward to running the tests.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Thanks Jordan — this aligns with our notes. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side:

1) Acceptance numbers:
- Latency: p95 target 200ms for the 13B latency-sensitive endpoint. For the 70B we accept p95 <= 450ms (we currently run it cold).
- Throughput: baseline throughput target 100 req/s for the 13B concurrent clients (sustained for 5m windows).
- Cost: the $1,200 per 1M tokens was our aggregated cost across infra and orchestration; if Redwood can demonstrate a 20% reduction in the same test patterns we’ll consider that successful.
- Quality: top-1 accuracy drop must be <= 5% on the primary eval shard; hallucination false-positive rate < 8% (we’ll provide labels).

2) Eval set: attached acme_js_eval_set.jsonl is the canonical set — we removed user PII. Use the first 1k entries for the initial runs.

3) Synthetic traffic: we’ll share a k6 script and a sample RPS profile (peaks at 220rps, regular at 40rps). Claire will drop the link in a follow-up email.

4) Security/access: we will provide a short-lived service account for the trial; send a scoping email to security@acme.ai for IP allowlisting.

We’re available for a kickoff Tuesday (Nov 9) 10–12 PT. Please send calendar invite and the Redwood run instructions.

Lee
